invalidForm: Some fields need a fix before saving. They’re marked below.

languages.title: Default languages
languages.intro: New sessions start with these. Each session can change them before it goes live.
languages.sourceHelp: Automatic detects English and Spanish sentence by sentence.
languages.targetsHelp: Viewers pick one of these on their phone.

providers.title: AI providers
providers.intro: Which models each provider uses. The Google API key is on the Providers and keys page.
providers.fallback: Switch to the other provider if one fails
providers.fallbackHelp: Captions keep going with the other provider instead of stopping.
providers.contextSentencesHelp: Earlier sentences sent along so the translation stays consistent (0–10).

network.title: Network
network.publicBaseUrlHelp: Used in links and QR codes instead of the LAN address, e.g. https://subs.example.org. Leave empty to use the LAN.
network.preferredInterfaceHelp: The address viewers’ phones use to reach this computer.

recording.title: Recording
recording.enabledByDefaultHelp: Keeps the audio so captions can be reviewed or reprocessed later.
recording.bitrateHelp: 32 kbps is plenty for speech and uses about 14 MB per hour.

obs.title: OBS
obs.websocketUrlHelp: Where to send captions for OBS’s own caption track. The password is on the Providers and keys page.

srt.title: SRT input
srt.enabledHelp: For a mixer or encoder that sends an SRT stream instead of using the capture page.
srt.latencyMsHelp: Higher values survive a worse network but add delay.

invalid.integer: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
invalid.url: Enter a full address starting with http:// or https://.
invalid.wsUrl: Enter a full address starting with ws:// or wss://.
invalid.languages: Pick at least one caption language.
invalid.server: The server didn’t accept this value.

banner.geminiBody: New sessions use Gemini by default because a valid Google API key is set.
banner.local: Using local: add a Google API key to use Gemini
banner.localInvalid: Using local: Google rejected the API key, so Gemini is off
banner.localBody: New sessions run on this computer with whisper and Ollama. Add a key below to switch to Gemini.
banner.mockBody: This is a development server: sessions show scripted captions.

google_api_key.title: Google API key
google_api_key.intro: Lets sessions use Gemini. Create one in Google AI Studio.

obs_websocket_password.title: OBS WebSocket password
obs_websocket_password.intro: Only needed to send captions to OBS’s own caption track.

srt_passphrase.title: SRT passphrase
srt_passphrase.intro: Encrypts audio sent over SRT from OBS, vMix or an encoder. Use 10 to 79 characters.

youtube_caption_url.title: YouTube caption URL
youtube_caption_url.intro: The ingestion URL from YouTube Live Control Room. Each session has its own; set it in the session.

keys.fieldHelp: Stored encrypted on this computer. It can’t be shown again, only replaced.
keys.envReadOnly: Set by an environment variable, so it can only be changed where the server is started.

tls.offNotice: HTTPS is off. Phones can still watch captions, but their browsers won’t allow the microphone on the capture page.
tls.installTitle: Trust the certificate on each device
tls.installIntro: This server signs its own certificate. Install its CA once on each phone or computer that opens the capture page, so the browser trusts it and allows the microphone. Viewers only watching captions don’t need it.
tls.notLocalCa: This certificate doesn’t come from this server’s CA, so there’s nothing to install: browsers already trust it, or you manage it yourself.
tls.checkFingerprint: If asked, check that the fingerprint matches the one above.

macos: Download the CA certificate and open the file: Keychain Access opens.
Add it to the “System” keychain and enter your Mac password.
In Keychain Access, double-click “Live Subtitles CA”, open Trust and set “When using this certificate” to “Always Trust”.
Close the window, enter your password again, and reload the page.
windows: Download the CA certificate and open the file.
Click “Install Certificate…”, choose “Local Machine” and continue.
Pick “Place all certificates in the following store”, then “Trusted Root Certification Authorities”.
Finish the wizard, accept the security warning, and restart the browser.
ios: Open this page in Safari and tap Download CA certificate, then Allow.
Open Settings › General › VPN & Device Management, tap the “Live Subtitles CA” profile and install it.
Go to Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings and turn on full trust for “Live Subtitles CA”.
Go back to Safari and reload the page.
android: Open Settings › Security › Encryption & credentials › Install a certificate › CA certificate (names vary by phone).
Tap “Install anyway”, pick the downloaded file and confirm with your screen lock.
Reopen Chrome and reload the page.
linux: Copy it into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ with a .crt name and run sudo update-ca-certificates (Debian, Ubuntu) or use trust anchor on Fedora.
Firefox and Chrome keep their own list: import it under Settings › Privacy & Security › Certificates › Authorities, and trust it for websites.
Restart the browser and reload the page.
